name: Lentil Bolognese
steps: Check that the spaghetti is eggless. Rinse the dry lentils and remove any stones. Simmer them in 900 ml water for 20–25 minutes until just tender but still holding their shape; drain any excess water. Finely dice onion, carrot and celery, mince garlic and tear basil leaves.

Heat 35 ml olive oil in a heavy wide pan over medium heat. Add onion, carrot and celery and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until softened and lightly golden. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute. Stir in tomato paste and oregano for 1 minute to deepen their flavour without scorching.

Add tomato passata, the cooked lentils, 150 ml water, 5 g salt and black pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 18–22 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and savoury but still moist. If it tightens before the carrot is soft, add some of the reserved 150 ml water. Fold in half the basil near the end; do not mash the lentils into a purée.

Meanwhile bring 2100 ml water and 8 g salt to a rolling boil. Cook spaghetti according to the packet until just al dente. Reserve 150 ml pasta water and drain. Toss the spaghetti into the sauce with 50–100 ml reserved pasta water for 1–2 minutes, so the tomato and lentils cling to the strands. Use more water only if the sauce is too thick.
Divide into four warm bowls. Spoon any remaining lentil sauce over the pasta, distribute the visible lentils and diced vegetables evenly, and finish with the remaining basil. Serve hot.
tips: The reviewed photo shows individual brown-green lentils in thick tomato sauce, small carrot and celery pieces and basil over spaghetti. Use green or brown lentils that retain their shape, not red lentils that dissolve. No meat, cheese or animal stock is included.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
